newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH PHONE CO MAY TRY TO KEEP SURFERS AT BAY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH PHONE CO MAY TRY TO KEEP SURFERS AT BAY.

text.p: The Finns' enthusiasm for the Internet is straining Helsinki telephone resources to the extent where the local operator is considering extra charges to keep surfers at bay, it said on Monday.
Helsinki telehone company Helsingin Puhelin Oy may start time-based local call fees at evenings and weekends to prevent surfers from hogging its line capacity, a spokesman said.

The telephone operator currently allows unlimited calling in off-peak hours, but Internet usage in its network doubled last year to 12 million minutes, he said. This corresponds to 57 people in the area being constantly connected.
Helsingin Puhelin said no decision has yet been made, but its owner HPY decided on Friday to allow time-based charges during off-peak hours, the spokesman said.

The biggest problem is students who dial up university Internet servers, paying less than about $0.10 in all for a whole weekend of surfing. Finland has one of the world's highest levels of Internet penetration.
